messages:
maya: kicked off a regional continuous-batcher sweep comparing H100 vs A100 across APAC/EU. focusing on window jitter, max_batch_tokens, and kernel selection. baseline is q4_0 quantized mosaic-13b.
jin: great — which metrics did you capture? latency p50/p95, tokens/sec, and quality delta?
maya: yup. p50/p95, tokens/s, kernel time breakdowns, and offline evals (perplexity + a small prompt set). attached short logs below.
bench-bot: RUN 2412345678 STARTED: cont-batch-sweep --model mosaic-13b-q4_0 --regions apac,eu --gpus h100,a100 --windows 10,20,40 --max_tokens 512,1024 --kernels fused,split
oscar: quick note — we saw earlier that increasing max_batch_tokens reduces p50 but hurts tail due to microburst queueing. watch the >95th percentile.
maya: exactly. raw highlights:
- H100 APAC window=20 max_tokens=512 fused kernel: p50 28ms, p95 190ms, tokens/s 7200
- A100 EU window=20 max_tokens=512 fused kernel: p50 42ms, p95 240ms, tokens/s 4500
- H100 APAC window=40 max_tokens=1024 split kernel: p50 34ms, p95 305ms, tokens/s 9200 (but p95 spikes)
- A100 EU window=10 max_tokens=512 fused kernel: p50 46ms, p95 210ms, tokens/s 3900
jin: interesting that split kernel pushes tokens/s higher on H100 but worsens p95. did you capture kernel-level counters?
maya: yes, kernel breakdown shows attention kernel time reduced by ~30% on H100 with split, but memcpy and concat ops increase, causing jitter when queue backpressure happens.
oscar: any fairness regressions across tenants? e.g., small vs large requests getting starved?
maya: ran a mixed cohort test (10% long, 90% short). with window=40 we see long requests get 2x higher tail latency on A100 EU. with window=10 fairness improves but throughput drops ~25%.
alyssa: what about quantization quality? any regressions from q4_0 on the eval set?
maya: small quality regression for some instruction-following prompts:
- baseline fp16 BLEU-ish proxy score: 0.78
- q4_0 overall: 0.75 (not huge) but certain calibration prompts drop by ~0.12
we suspect kernel fp accumulation differences when split kernel + q4 path used.
jin: could be numeric drift due to accumulation order. can you reproduce with deterministic seed and single-batch run?
maya: repro snippet I used:
```
python bench/run_infer.py --model mosaic-13b-q4_0 --prompt-file samples/edge_prompts.json --batch 1 --seed 42 --kernel split
```
results were consistent across runs on H100. on A100 variance higher.
oscar: ops idea: add small microbatch drain timeout to reduce jitter for split kernel. eg reduce batch window to 15 and add max_wait_ms=8.
maya: tried that: window=15 + max_wait_ms=8 on H100 APAC gave p50 30ms p95 210ms tokens/s 8100 — good middle ground.
alyssa: any recommendations for default config per region/gpu?
maya: provisional:
- H100 (global): window=20, max_batch_tokens=512, prefer split kernel for throughput but set max_wait_ms=8
- A100 (eu): window=12, max_batch_tokens=512, prefer fused kernel to keep p95 reasonable
- For mixed-tenant workloads: default window=12 and enable cohort-aware slotting
jin: will add these to the config repo. PR incoming with perf numbers + commands.
bench-bot: RUN 2412345678 COMPLETE: succeeded. artifacts -> s3://redwood-bench/2412345678/
oscar: thanks maya. next step: run a long-duration 24h probe on peak-sim traffic to validate tail behavior.
maya: on it. will kick that off tomorrow and tag results here :eyes:
